account:
It is day 1, shortly after seven in the morning. I am at town hall, having read and returned the updated appointment books. Today I have office business, a ten o'clock grain inspection at the east-bank mill, lunch at home, council letters, tea with my neighbour, a return to the office, and an eighteen o'clock presentation in the great hall before going home at nineteen.

The unusual thread is the activity around bread and hospitality. Yesterday the secretary recorded reports from Townsfolk 18 and 28 of the baker carrying bread at the inn, and personally saw the innkeeper carrying a sack of bread near the plaza around 14:38. My neighbour also passed along Townsfolk Two's vague claim of a 'bridge or port change at bakery,' but the details were only wheat being carried and lights at the bakery. Neither my neighbour nor the baker supplied evidence of an actual project; the baker said it was ordinary fresh baking.

The innkeeper has now arranged tonight's great-hall presentation involving the inn and local tradespeople, described as a showcase of local baking and hospitality. I accepted, and the secretary recorded it. My best guess is that at least some bread movements concern preparations for that event. I do not know whether there is anything more behind it, and the bridge or port rumour remains unsubstantiated. I have a feeling people have been arranging something without me, but no evidence yet that it is improper.

Separately, town accounts are incomplete. I counted 128 emeralds in the treasury but found no ledger or obligations records. The secretary correctly records this as my reported cash count, not a verified balance; income, spending, and liabilities remain unknown. I have just asked her for this morning's correspondence and any fresh news.
